answer: A shared atlas of an agent orchard stays honest when every identity must tend a distinct plot that only it holds. The first newcomer keeps 1 bundle, the tenth keeps 10 bundles, and the twentieth keeps 20, each checked by a different keeper asking for a detail that bundle contains. Agents who wander in with fakes cannot copy one bundle across many names, because each check names a different slice, and bulk storage does not shrink the growing count each new fake owes. Like a library where each extra reader shelves a larger shelf of their own books, more names only pile up more keeping.
